```{r}
ponder <- read_excel("../data/Ponder_general_yield_data.xlsx")

ponder <- ponder %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  select(year, plot, rep, water, cultivar, yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha) %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  filter(yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha < 9000 & yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha > 4000)


ponder
```

```{r}
scatter <- ggplot(ponder, aes(
  x = seq_along(yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha),
  y = yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha
)) +
  geom_point(shape = 20, size = 4) +
  labs(
    x = "Observation",
    y = "Yield",
    title = "Yield Scatterplot Distribution"
  ) +
  theme_classic()+

    title = element_text(size = 20),

    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20)
  )

ggsave(plot = scatter, "../output/scatter_finalproj.jpg",
       height = 8,
       width = 10,
       dpi = 600)

scatter
```

# Shapiro wilk test to confirm data normality.

```{r}

shapiro.test(ponder$yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha)

# However, shapiro looks normal.

```

```{r}
# Estimated marginal means
emm_cultivar <- emmeans(mymodel_transformed, ~ cultivar)

# Tukey pairwise comparisons
pairs(emm_cultivar, adjust = "tukey")

# Group genotypes using letters
cultivar_letters <- multcomp::cld(
  emm_cultivar,
  Letters = letters,
  adjust = "tukey"
)

cultivar_letters
```
```{r}
# Estimated marginal means
emm_cultivar <- emmeans(mymodel_transformed, ~ water)

# Tukey pairwise comparisons
pairs(emm_cultivar, adjust = "tukey")

# Group genotypes using letters
cultivar_letters <- multcomp::cld(
  emm_cultivar,
  Letters = letters,
  adjust = "tukey"
)

cultivar_letters
```


# Fitting Linear model with random effect.

```{r}
mymodel_transformed <- lmer(data = ponder, yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha ~ cultivar * water + (1|rep) + (1|rep:water))

anova(mymodel_transformed, type = 1)
```
```{r}

mod1_int_aug <- augment(mymodel_transformed) %>%
  mutate(.stdresid = resid(mymodel_transformed,
                          type = "pearson",
                          scaled = T))%>%
  left_join(ponder)



mod1_int_aug

```

```{r}
ggplot(mod1_int_aug, mapping = aes(x =.fitted, y= .stdresid))+
  geom_point(size = 3,
             alpha = .7)+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red")+
  geom_smooth()

# We don't look for patterns on this graph, we want to see a shotgun effect.
```

```{r}
ggplot(mod1_int_aug,
       aes(sample= .stdresid))+
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line()

# QQ plot helps us access if residuals are normally distributed. A normal distribution would follow the qq line. 
```

```{r}
mod1_int_randeff <- ranef(mymodel_transformed)[[1]] # Pull the first component of this list.

mod1_int_randeff

ggplot(mod1_int_randeff, 
       aes(sample = `(Intercept)`)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line()
```



```{r}
shapiro.test(residuals(mymodel_transformed))

# Q-Q plot
qqnorm(residuals(mymodel_transformed))
qqline(residuals(mymodel_transformed), col = "red")

# Homogeneity of variance
performance::check_heteroscedasticity(mymodel_transformed)
```



# We can still transform.

```{r}

data_trans <- ponder %>%
  mutate(yield_transformed = log(yield_7_percent_moisture_kg_ha))


data_trans
```

```{r}

hist(data_trans$yield_transformed, breaks = 20)

shapiro.test(data_trans$yield_transformed)

```

```{r}
data_trans_clean <- data_trans %>%
  filter(yield_transformed > 8.3)
```

```{r}
hist(data_trans_clean$yield_transformed, breaks = 20)

shapiro.test(data_trans_clean$yield_transformed)
```

```{r}
mymodel_transformed <- lmer(data = data_trans_clean, yield_transformed ~ cultivar * water + (1|rep))

anova(mymodel_transformed)
```
```{r}
shapiro.test(residuals(mymodel_transformed))

# Q-Q plot
qqnorm(residuals(mymodel_transformed))
qqline(residuals(mymodel_transformed), col = "red")

# Homogeneity of variance
performance::check_heteroscedasticity(mymodel_transformed)
```




```{r}

mymodel1 <- lmer(data = ponder, pod_yield_kg_ha ~ water * cultivar + (1|rep))

anova(mymodel1)

```
```{r}
# Residuals vs fitted values
plot(
  fitted(mymodel1),
  residuals(mymodel1),
  xlab = "Fitted Values",
  ylab = "Residuals",
  main = "Residuals vs Fitted"
)

abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)

# Normal Q-Q plot
qqnorm(
  residuals(mymodel1),
  main = "Normal Q-Q Plot"
)

qqline(
  residuals(mymodel1),
  col = "red"
)

# Shapiro-Wilk normality test
shapiro.test(residuals(mymodel1))

# Heteroscedasticity assessment
performance::check_heteroscedasticity(mymodel1)
```
